name: World Border
desc: Updates the world border (center, size, warning distance/buffer, damping).

writeup.p: World border state machine with six actions: SET_SIZE, LERP_SIZE, SET_CENTER, INITIALIZE, SET_WARNING_TIME and SET_WARNING_BLOCKS. ServerConfigurationManager broadcasts the five change actions to all players on border mutation (lines 245-261 in the MCP builds) and sends INITIALIZE to each player on join (line 786). INITIALIZE is the only action carrying the full state: center, current and target diameter, transition time, and both warning values.

The client handler func_175093_a delegates to packet.func_179788_a(worldBorder), which mutates the single WorldBorder object owned by the client world: setCenter, setTransition, setWarningDistance and setWarningTime. The border then feeds the renderer's red vignette and the camera clamp in EntityRenderer. It is one of the few packets whose handler mutates shared world state instead of copying values into local fields.

No module in the 8 clients references S44. Border tracking would matter for movement modules pathing around a shrinking border or for border-bypass claims, but none exists in the corpus. The border is server-enforced: EntityPlayerMP movement validation and WorldBorder.intersects run server-side and teleport or damage players who cross it, so the client's copy is purely cosmetic and modules gain nothing by intercepting it.

All six actions deserialize doubles and a VarLong transition time with no sanity bounds; a hostile server can inject NaN or extreme diameters into the client WorldBorder, which the renderer then lerps against, producing visual glitches (the classic NaN border). Because enforcement is server-side, corrupting the client border changes nothing gameplay-relevant. The notable quirk is LERP_SIZE's VarLong time field, which is milliseconds server-side, not ticks.

implementation.overview: Six-action world border state machine, broadcast on change and fully initialized on join. Server-enforced, so the client copy is cosmetic; none of the 8 clients has a module that references it. The interesting wire details are the mixed field widths and the VarLong transition time.
implementation.server_handling: ServerConfigurationManager registers a WorldBorder listener that broadcasts SET_SIZE, LERP_SIZE, SET_CENTER, SET_WARNING_TIME and SET_WARNING_BLOCKS to all players on mutation (lines 245-261, MCP numbering), and sends INITIALIZE in initializeConnectionToPlayer (line 786). INITIALIZE serializes the whole border: center X/Z doubles, diameter and target doubles, VarLong transition time, warning distance and warning time ints.
implementation.protocol_notes: Action is a VarInt enum; payload depends on action. SET_SIZE: one double (target diameter). LERP_SIZE: old diameter double, target double, VarLong transition time in milliseconds. SET_CENTER: two doubles. SET_WARNING_TIME and SET_WARNING_BLOCKS: one int each. INITIALIZE: center doubles, both diameters, VarLong, and both warning ints. readEnumValue can return null on an out-of-range action, which NPEs in the read switch.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat measures border packets. The server enforces the border in its own movement pipeline (EntityPlayerMP position validation against WorldBorder.intersects), so client-side border state has no bearing on any server-side check. The only client-visible effect of tampering is rendering artifacts.
